newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bomb kills three, more Algerian massacres reported.
newsitem.headline: Bomb kills three, more Algerian massacres reported.

text.p: A bomb killed three people in Algeria's southern city of M'Sila on Monday and four people had their throats cut by Moslem rebels, Algerian newspapers said on Wednesday.
El Watan said the bombing was the latest attack by Moslem rebels in a region where according to residents more than 60 people had been killed in attacks on isolated villages this month.
There was no official confirmation of the attacks by the authorities. El Watan, usually well-informed on security issues, also appeared hesitant to give an exact figure for the village raids.
The newspaper said about 30 Moslem guerrillas attacked Dairat Labguer hamlet near M'Sila town, 180 km (110 miles) south of Algiers, last week.

"According to eyewitnesses, the massacre reportedly left about 50 people dead," the newspaper said adding that the assailants cut the throats of the peasants, slaughtered their sheep and cows and stole the women's jewels.
Four women kidnapped during the massacre were later found dead with their throats slashed, El Watan said.
The newspaper said 17 people, including eight women, were slaughtered five days earlier at another village some five km (three miles) away.
Guerrillas detonated a bomb in downtown M'Sila on Monday killing three passers-by, the newspaper said.
Another newspaper, Al Khabar, said that the same day, rebels cut the throats of four people in Al Azharia village near Chlef, 150 km (95 miles) southwest of Algiers.
The killing took place shortly after the security forces reopened a nearby road which had been closed by guerrillas, it added.

The reported recent flare-up in violence followed the June 5 general election which President Liamine Zeroual and legal opposition parties hope will help pacify the North African country after more than five years of violence.
About 60,000 people have been killed in Algeria's violence since 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a huge lead.
The authorities barred radical Islamists from this month's election but allowed two moderate Islamist parties to compete. These won a total of 103 seats in the 380-member National Assembly.
The main legal Islamist party, Movement of a Peaceful Society, is expected to join a three-party coalition government led by Prime Minister Ahmed Ouyahia.
Ouyahia is the leading figure in the National Democratic Rally which groups Zeroual's supporters and which has 156 seats in the National Assembly.
